entities.summary: Tielman Susato was a Renaissance composer, instrumentalist and publisher of music in Antwerp. Born in the 1530s, Susato rose to prominence in the 1560s as a leading figure in the development of polyphonic music. His compositions, which often featured complex harmonies and innovative instrumental arrangements, were widely performed in courts across Europe. Susato's publishing house, which he founded with his brother, became a major force in the music industry, producing scores for a wide range of genres, from secular songs to sacred music. Susato's legacy extends beyond his own compositions, as he played a significant role in shaping the musical landscape of the Renaissance. His influence can be seen in the works of later composers, such as William Byrd and Orlando Gibbons, who built upon Susato's innovations. Susato's contributions to music publishing also paved the way for the development of the modern music industry. Despite his significant impact on the development of Western classical music, Susato's life remains somewhat of a mystery, and much of what we know about him comes from his own music and the accounts of his contemporaries.
